answer: A beacon registry can anchor sybil resistance: every agent that wants to join an economy must first publish a verifiable work credential — a lantern of proof tied to a real, costly computation or a stake that is slashed on fraud. New identities start with near-zero trust and must complete a slow voyage of small, attested tasks before earning full trading rights. Creating a hundred fake agents then costs a hundred times the stake and the compute, while honest newcomers pay only once, so mass forgery becomes unprofitable and the network stays open to genuine participants.
